26: /-- Hamming distance is non-increasing under inner composition with an injective function.
27: NOTE : we can prove strict equality given `g` being an equivalence instead of injection.
28: -/
29: theorem hammingDist_le_of_outer_comp_injective {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [Fintype ι₂]
30:     {β : ι₂ → Type*} [∀ i, DecidableEq (β i)] [DecidableEq ι₂]
31:     (x y : ∀ i, β i) (g : ι₁ → ι₂) (hg : Function.Injective g) :
32:     hammingDist (fun i => x (g i)) (fun i => y (g i)) ≤ hammingDist x y := by
33:   -- Let D₂ be the set of disagreeing indices for x and y.
34:   let D₂ := Finset.filter (fun i₂ => x i₂ ≠ y i₂) Finset.univ
35:   -- The Hamming distance of the composed functions is the card of the preimage of D₂.
36:   suffices (Finset.filter (fun i₁ => x (g i₁) ≠ y (g i₁)) Finset.univ).card ≤ D₂.card by
37:     unfold hammingDist; simp only [this, D₂]
38:   -- The cardinality of a preimage is at most the cardinalit
39:     -- of the original set for an injective function.
40:   -- ⊢ #{i₁ | x (g i₁) ≠ y (g i₁)} ≤ #D₂
41:    -- First, we state that the set on the left is the `preimage` of D₂ under g.
42:   have h_preimage : Finset.filter (fun i₁ => x (g i₁) ≠ y (g i₁)) Finset.univ
43:     = D₂.preimage g (by exact hg.injOn) := by
44:     -- Use `ext` to prove equality by showing the membership conditions are the same.
45:     ext i₁
46:     -- Now `simp` can easily unfold `mem_filter` and `mem_preimage` and see they are equivalent.
47:     simp only [ne_eq, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, mem_preimage, D₂]
48: 
49:   -- Now, rewrite the goal using `preimage`.
50:   rw [h_preimage]
51:   set D₁ := D₂.preimage g (by exact hg.injOn)
52:   -- ⊢ #D₁ ≤ #D₂
53:   -- Step 1 : The size of a set is at most the size of its image under an injective function.
54:   have h_card_le_image : D₁.card ≤ (D₁.image g).card := by
55:     -- This follows directly from the fact that `g` is injective on the set D₁.
56:     apply Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (f := g)
57:     · -- Goal 1 : Prove that `g` maps `D₁` to `D₁.image g`. This is true by definition of image.
58:       have res := Set.mapsTo_image (f := g) (s := D₁)
59:       convert res
60:       simp only [coe_image]
61:       -- (D₁.image g : Set ι₂)
62:     · -- Goal 2 : Prove that `g` is injective on the set `D₁`.
63:       -- This is true because our main hypothesis `hg` states that `g` is injective everywhere.
64:       exact Function.Injective.injOn hg
65: 
66:   -- Step 2 : The image of the preimage of a set is always a subset of the original set.
67:   have h_image_subset : D₁.image g ⊆ D₂ := by
68:     simp [D₁, Finset.image_preimage]
69: 
70:   -- Step 3 : By combining these two facts, we get our result.
71:   -- |D₁| ≤ |image g(D₁)| (from Step 1)
72:   -- and |image g(D₁)| ≤ |D₂| (since it's a subset)
73:   exact h_card_le_image.trans (Finset.card_le_card h_image_subset)
